crops.name: Rice (paddy)
crops.summary: The principal food crop of Manipur, grown mainly as kharif (monsoon-season) paddy in the valley and on terraces and jhum fields in the hills. LouNgak AI's first monitoring target.

sections.title: Importance in Manipur
items: Staple food crop of the state; the valley districts (Imphal East, Imphal West, Thoubal, Bishnupur, Kakching) hold most of the wet-rice area.
Area and production figures: SOURCE_NEEDED (Manipur Department of Agriculture / data.gov.in district statistics).

sections.title: Season and crop calendar (valley, kharif)
items: Nursery: about May-June. Transplanting: about June-July. Harvest: about October-November.

Dates vary with elevation, variety and rainfall onset; a district crop calendar from the Department of Agriculture or ICAR Research Complex for NEH Region (Manipur Centre) is needed before these dates drive any rule.

sections.title: Growth stages
items: Vegetative phase: germination, seedling, tillering, stem elongation.
Reproductive phase: panicle initiation, booting, heading, flowering.
Ripening phase: milk, dough, mature grain.

sections.title: Common pests
items: Yellow stem borer (Scirpophaga incertulas): dead hearts at tillering, white ears at heading.
Rice leaf folder (Cnaphalocrocis medinalis): folded leaves with scraped, whitish streaks.
Rice gall midge (Orseolia oryzae): tubular 'silver shoot' galls instead of panicles.
Brown planthopper (Nilaparvata lugens): 'hopper burn', circular patches of drying plants.
Regional prevalence in Manipur: SOURCE_NEEDED (no public Manipur surveillance dataset was found; see the source assessment).

sections.title: Common diseases
items: Blast (Magnaporthe oryzae): spindle-shaped leaf lesions; neck blast breaks the panicle neck.
Bacterial leaf blight (Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae): wavy yellowing from the leaf tips and margins.
Sheath blight (Rhizoctonia solani): oval greenish-grey lesions on the leaf sheath near the water line.
Brown spot (Bipolaris oryzae): small oval brown spots on leaves and grains.

sections.title: Weather sensitivities
items: Long leaf-wetness and high humidity favour blast; LouNgak's blast weather rule is a PLACEHOLDER awaiting agronomist review.
Heavy rain at flowering and harvest can cause lodging and grain loss; prolonged submergence damages young transplants.

sections.title: Management
items: Follow the IPM Package for Rice and local KVK advice: field scouting, economic threshold levels (ETL, Table 3.1.2 of the package) and recommended practices.
LouNgak AI does not recommend pesticides or doses.

can: Vegetation vigour (NDVI) of clear land in monitored zones against the same dates in earlier years (Sentinel-2).

Weather conducive to blast or brown planthopper under PLACEHOLDER rules (a watch, not a detection).

crops.name: Chak-hao (black rice of Manipur)
crops.scientific_name: Oryza sativa L. (aromatic, glutinous black-pericarp landraces)
crops.summary: Scented, glutinous black rice of Manipur, registered as a Geographical Indication. Profiled separately from rice because its value, varieties and markets differ; its agronomy and pests follow rice.

sections.title: Geographical Indication
items: Registered as a Geographical Indication ('Chak-Hao') in 2020. The application number and registered proprietor are to be confirmed in the GI Journal.

sections.title: Characteristics
items: Black to purple grain from anthocyanin pigments in the bran; aromatic and glutinous (sticky) when cooked.
Traditionally used for festive dishes such as chak-hao kheer (rice pudding).

sections.title: Varieties
items: Named Chak-hao landraces differ by district and community; list only varieties documented by CAU Imphal, ICAR RC NEH Manipur Centre or the GI dossier.

sections.title: Season, growth stages, pests and diseases
items: Grown in the kharif season like other valley paddy; see the Rice profile for growth stages, pests and diseases.
Landrace-specific susceptibility (for example to blast or lodging): SOURCE_NEEDED.

can: The same zone-level observations as rice.
cannot: Distinguish Chak-hao fields from other paddy from space.
Assess grain quality, aroma or GI compliance.

crops.name: Maize
crops.summary: Grown in Manipur's hill and valley districts, often on upland and jhum fields. LouNgak AI's second monitoring priority after rice.

sections.title: Importance and distribution in Manipur
items: District area, seasons and main uses: SOURCE_NEEDED (Manipur Department of Agriculture / district statistics).

sections.title: Growth stages
items: Vegetative: emergence (VE), leaf stages (V1 to Vn), tasselling (VT).
Reproductive: silking (R1), blister (R2), milk (R3), dough (R4), dent (R5), physiological maturity (R6).

sections.title: Common pests
items: Fall armyworm (Spodoptera frugiperda): an invasive pest first reported in India in 2018; ragged feeding holes and sawdust-like frass in the whorl.
Maize stem borer (Chilo partellus): shot holes in leaves, dead hearts in young plants.
Regional prevalence in Manipur: SOURCE_NEEDED.

sections.title: Common diseases
items: Turcicum leaf blight (Exserohilum turcicum): long cigar-shaped grey-green lesions.
Maydis leaf blight (Bipolaris maydis): smaller tan lesions between the veins.
Common rust (Puccinia sorghi): brick-red pustules on both leaf surfaces.

sections.title: Management
items: Follow ICAR-IIMR and KVK advisories, including the national fall armyworm advisories. LouNgak AI does not recommend pesticides or doses.

can: Zone-level vegetation vigour and weather context, as for rice, where maize grows inside a monitored zone.
cannot: Locate maize fields (no crop map is loaded); maize-specific weather rules are not yet defined.
